verdict.rationale: Cal.com publishes an official open-source edition, Cal.diy, under the MIT license on its GitHub org. However, it is a fork with all enterprise and commercial code removed, so the full Cal.com product's source is not open: community reports describe a move to closed source, and Cal.diy drops Teams, Organizations, Workflows, SSO and similar features. missing for 10: open-license source for the full Cal.com product including enterprise features, and first-party docs confirming the main Cal.com repository's current license status.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Cal.diy is 100% MIT-licensed with no proprietary "Enterprise Edition" features.
Cal.diy is the community-driven, fully open-source scheduling platform — a fork of Cal.com with all enterprise/commercial code removed.
Cal.com's differentiators are the self-hostable MIT edition (Cal.diy)
Cal.diy removes Teams, Organizations, Insights, Workflows, SSO/SAML and other EE-only features.
